newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Canberra to consider rabbit industry compensation.
newsitem.headline: Canberra to consider rabbit industry compensation.

text.p: The Australian government said on Wednesday it would consider compensation for the wild rabbit industry as a result of the accidental release of rabbit calicivirus disease (RCD) in 1995.

Science Minister Peter McGauran said in a statement the government did not accept that it was legally liable for the accidental release, but it acknowledged that a small number of businesses may have been unprepared for the premature release.
"The settlement proposal now being implemented recognises that while most people continue to benefit from RCD, a small minority may have been temporarily disadvantaged," he said.
Rabbit numbers have dropped sharply particularly in dry areas since its official release last October.
Farmers have blamed rabbits for causing hundreds of millions of dollars of damage to crops and for driving native animals and plants to the verge of extinction.
